title: Effects of Dialogue Corpora Properties on Fine-Tuning a Moshi-Based Spoken Dialogue Model
observations: Authors study Japanese continuation after a10second audio prompt, not zero-context English character adaptation.
All reported models share69k-hour J-Chat adaptation and115-hour final task data; their data scale far exceeds our small synthetic corpus.
Intermediate formal-speech corpus gave their best coherence; combining all intermediate corpora did not improve it further.
Reported evaluation uses NISQA and LLM judging, not an independent human quality rating.
inference_for_our_work: Treat timing profile and context duration as dataset properties to measure. More mixture components need not improve coherence. This source does not establish our text-only transfer hypothesis or a sufficient small-data recipe.
official_note: README warns shorter training duration can cause earlier silence at inference. Our short synthetic clips therefore warrant a duration-distribution audit rather than relying on joint loss.
